content: Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can increase the toxicity of ibutilide by prolonging the QTc interval. It is essential to use these agents with caution and monitor the patient closely. For patients at higher risk of severe cardiac arrhythmias, consider performing pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can enhance the toxicity of ifosfamide through mechanisms related to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. This co-administration may elevate the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Exercise caution and monitor the patient carefully. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can increase the toxicity of iloperidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Additionally, they may enhance the effects of iloperidone through an unknown mechanism. Close monitoring is advised. When magnesium sulfate is used with CNS depressants, particularly at higher doses, there is an increased risk of enhanced central nervous system depression. Patients should be closely monitored for signs of excessive sedation or respiratory depression. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can increase the effects of imipramine through an unknown mechanism. Patients should be monitored for potential seizures, especially when using higher doses of magnesium sulfate with drugs that lower the seizure threshold. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can increase the toxicity of indomethacin, insulin aspart, insulin aspart protamine, insulin degludec, insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, inhaled insulin, insulin isophane human, insulin regular human, and insulin lispro through mechanisms related to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. This co-administration may elevate the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can decrease the levels of iron dextran complex and iron sucrose by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. To avoid chelation with magnesium, administer iron products at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can increase the toxicity of isoniazid, irbesartan, losartan, and lisinopril through mechanisms related to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. This co-administration may elevate the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can increase the effects of loxapine and lurasidone through unknown mechanisms. Patients should be closely monitored for signs of enhanced CNS depression when these agents are used together. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can increase the toxicity of methadone, macimorelin, and lenvatinib by prolonging the QTc interval. For patients at higher risk of severe cardiac arrhythmias, consider performing pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can decrease the levels of levofloxacin, levothyroxine, and minocycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. To avoid chelation with magnesium, administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose. For levothyroxine, administer at least 4 hours after each dose. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can increase the toxicity of ketoconazole, levoketoconazole, and moexipril through mechanisms related to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. This co-administration may elevate the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can increase the toxicity of ketoprofen, ketorolac (including intranasal forms), lanthanum carbonate, meclofenamate, mefenamic acid, meloxicam, methyclothiazide, and methylprednisolone through mechanisms related to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. This co-administration may elevate the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can increase the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval. For patients at higher risk of severe cardiac arrhythmias, consider performing pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride can increase the toxicity of mannitol and magaldrate through mechanisms related to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. This co-administration may elevate the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor the patient closely.
